units.text: Aspose.Email FOSS for Python reads .msg, .eml, and .txt files, writes .msg files, and converts between these formats. It reads .msg files using the CFB format and provides classes to parse and write message structures. It supports MAPI message objects through the MapiMessage class, which can be created from scratch, loaded from files, or converted to and from email messages.
It reads Outlook .msg files and Compound File Binary (CFB) containers using CFBReader, supporting file paths and raw bytes, with directory traversal, path resolution, and stream data extraction.
It writes Outlook .msg files and Compound File Binary (CFB) containers using CFBWriter, enabling programmatic creation of CFB documents and direct serialization to bytes or files.
It converts between Outlook .msg and standard .eml formats by transforming MapiMessage objects to EmailMessage instances and vice versa, preserving message content and structure.

It creates and edits messages through MapiMessage, supporting subject, body, recipients, attachments, MAPI properties, and named properties, with methods for adding attachments and saving to .msg files.
It provides low-level access to Compound File Binary structures through CFBDocument, CFBStorage, and CFBReader, enabling manual construction, traversal, and inspection of storages and streams.
It offers low-level Outlook .msg document access through MsgReader, MsgDocument, and MsgWriter, supporting direct parsing of property streams and subobject streams for detailed message inspection.
The first example reads a MSG file and prints its subject line using the MapiMessage class.
The second example creates a new MSG file with sender, recipient, and attachment properties, saves it, then loads and exports it to EML format.
The following workflows demonstrate converting messages between MSG and EML formats, and reading structured storage streams.
Convert MSG to EML using MapiMessage and email message APIs.
Convert EML to MSG using email parser and MapiMessage APIs.
Read structured storage streams using CFB APIs.

Aspose.Email FOSS for Python provides high-level MSG and low-level MSG and CFB APIs for reading, writing, and converting email formats. The high-level MSG API centers on MapiMessage for message creation, editing, and conversion, while the low-level MSG API uses MsgReader and MsgWriter for direct property-stream access, and the low-level CFB API uses CFBReader and CFBWriter for raw Compound File Binary container access.

The MapiMessage class provides methods to create messages from scratch, load them from files or email messages, and convert them to MSG or EML formats, as well as to inspect and modify properties, recipients, and attachments.
The CFBReader class enables reading raw Compound File Binary data from bytes or files, providing access to directory entries, streams, and storages through iteration and path resolution methods.
The CFBWriter class provides class methods to serialize a CFBDocument into bytes or write it directly to a file.
The MsgReader class parses MSG files at the property-stream level, exposing the underlying CFBReader, storage layout, and methods to iterate over recipients, attachments, and property streams.
The MsgWriter class provides class methods to serialize a MsgDocument into bytes or write it directly to a file.

It adds broader mail-server connectivity and format coverage — IMAP/SMTP/POP3, TNEF parsing and generation, a dedicated calendar/appointment API, and direct EML file parsing — plus commercial support.
MapiPropertyCollection class provides methods to add, get, set, remove, and iterate over MAPI properties, with methods add, get, set, remove, and iter_properties.
